hints: Use the given exact trigonometric ratios: with $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$ we have $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$, and with $\sin\theta = \frac{8}{17}$ we have $\cos\theta = \frac{15}{17}$.
Resolve the three forces along the direction of the $30\text{ N}$ force ($x$-axis) and perpendicular to it ($y$-axis).
Find the resultant magnitude using $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$ and the angle using $\tan\beta = \frac{Y}{X}$.
walkthrough:
State the exact trigonometric ratios for angles $\alpha$ and $\theta$ using Pythagoras theorem:
- Since $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$, the adjacent side is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12$, so $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$.
- Since $\sin\theta = \frac{8}{17}$, the adjacent side is $\sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{289 - 64} = \sqrt{225} = 15$, so $\cos\theta = \frac{15}{17}$.
Choose a Cartesian coordinate system with the positive $x$-axis aligned along the $30\text{ N}$ force and the positive $y$-axis perpendicular to it pointing upwards.

Resolve all three forces horizontally to find the resultant component $X$:
$$X = 30 - 34\sin\theta - 26\sin\alpha$$
Substitute the exact fractions:
$$X = 30 - 34\left(\frac{8}{17}\right) - 26\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)$$
Simplify each fraction:
$$34 \times \frac{8}{17} = 2 \times 8 = 16$$
$$26 \times \frac{5}{13} = 2 \times 5 = 10$$
Compute $X$:
$$X = 30 - 16 - 10 = 4\text{ N}$$

Resolve all three forces vertically to find the resultant component $Y$:
$$Y = 34\cos\theta - 26\cos\alpha$$
Substitute the exact fractions:
$$Y = 34\left(\frac{15}{17}\right) - 26\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)$$
Simplify each fraction:
$$34 \times \frac{15}{17} = 2 \times 15 = 30$$
$$26 \times \frac{12}{13} = 2 \times 12 = 24$$
Compute $Y$:
$$Y = 30 - 24 = 6\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R$ using the Pythagorean theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{52}$$
Simplify the surd:
$$R = \sqrt{4 \times 13} = 2\sqrt{13} \approx 7.2111\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives $R = 7.21\text{ N}$.

Calculate the angle $\beta$ that the resultant makes with the positive $x$-axis (the $30\text{ N}$ force):
$$\tan\beta = \frac{Y}{X} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5$$
$$\beta = \arctan(1.5) \approx 56.31^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place gives $\beta = 56.3^\circ$ measured anticlockwise above the $30\text{ N}$ force.
